refuted.finding: The Unsupported.csproj group row shows only the Provisional label badge and the count. The artboard's Unsupported.csproj header also draws the warning-outlined "Unsupported" badge before "provisional", so the sidebar drops the badge that matters most and keeps the lower-priority Provisional pill. The message leaf below still states the reason, so no information is lost.
refuted.reason: The crop shows the Unsupported.csproj group row with a Provisional pill and the count 3. But the reference artboard is the 1200 px main panel, and the same box there is its Serilog row, so it is another surface. Design System §9 gives the sidebar's unsupported state as sidebar-unsupported (the message leaf) with no group-row badge, and the hard DS-STATE-1 reads 'present: ... sidebar-installed-unsupported-unsupported.csproj; missing: none'.

refuted.finding: The trailing counts in this pane end on two columns. The Installed pane header's count "46" ends at x 290, 10 px from the pane edge. Every project group row's count (0, 2, 3, 13) ends at x 282, 8 px further in, because the tree rows keep clear of the 8 px scrollbar at x 292 to 299 and the header does not. In the artboard all trailing counts in the list column share one end edge.
refuted.reason: The crop does show '46' ending further right than the group counts (DS-OVERFLOW-2: '46' 263.3–290 in a box ending at 296; group counts end at 282 in boxes ending at 288). Each end meets its own declared rule, though: hard DS-INSET-3 reads 'section headers 6 (target 6); group rows 6 ×4 (target 6)'. The 8 px offset is the scrollbar gutter that DS-SCROLL-1 declares ('[sidebar-installed-list] 8'), and the artboard compared with is the main panel, another surface.

refuted.finding: The Unsupported.csproj group row shows only a 'Provisional' label badge and its count. The artboard's Unsupported.csproj header draws an 'Unsupported' warning label badge before the provisional badge, so the group row's unsupported badge is missing. The message leaf below still names the condition, so no information is lost.
refuted.reason: The cited rule DS-STATE-1 is measured hard as 'present: sidebar-installed-empty-empty.csproj, sidebar-installed-unsupported-unsupported.csproj; missing: none', and the crop shows the unsupported message leaf under the row. The 'Unsupported' badge appears only on the main-panel artboard (a 1200 px surface whose same box holds a different row), and the sidebar's §9 contract names no such badge.

refuted.finding: The three package rows under Unsupported.csproj (Newtonsoft.Json, Polly, Serilog) show only name and version. The artboard draws a 'Read-only' status on each of these rows, and the capture has no read-only marker in the version slot. The unresolved Serilog row above does use that slot for its 'unresolved' status.
refuted.reason: The crop shows compact 22 px sidebar rows (Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.3, Polly 8.4.2, Serilog 3.1.1) with only a name and a version. The artboard's 'Read-only' sits in the meta line of the main panel's comfortable rows (author · Read-only), on another surface with another row form. The sidebar's read-only condition is stated by the unsupported message leaf above these rows, so neither a rule nor a sidebar spec element requires a per-row marker.
